passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: The following discussion and analysis should be read together with our audited consolidated financial statements and notes appearing in Item 18 below. General Critical Accounting Policies and Estimates Our significant accounting policies are described in Item 18. Financial Statements – Note 2. Our results of operations and financial condition are based on our consolidated financial statements, which are presented in conformity with United States generally accepted accounting principles (U.S. GAAP). The preparation of the consolidated financial statements requires management to select accounting policies, and to make estimates, assumptions and judgments that involve the accounting policies described below that affect the amounts reported in the consolidated financial statements. Significant changes in assumptions and/or conditions and changes in our critical accounting policies could materially impact our operating results and financial condition. We believe our most critical accounting policies relate to: • Revenue Recognition; • Impairment of Long-Lived Assets and Goodwill; • Income Taxes; • Post-employment Benefits Liabilities. Revenue Recognition We generate revenues primarily from fixed-price long-term contracts involving the design, development, manufacture and integration of defense systems and products. In addition, to a lesser extent, we provide non-defense systems and products as well as support and services for our systems and products. Revenues from our contracts are principally recognized using the Financial Accounting Standards Board (FASB), Accounting Standards Codification (ASC) 606. We assess contractual arrangements at inception according to the five-step model of ASC 606. We recognize revenues for each of the identified performance obligations when our customer obtains control of the products or services. The assessment of when the customer obtains control involves significant judgments, including, inter alia, whether there is an alternative use for a product, the contract terms, assessment of the enforceable rights for payments, and technical or contractual constraints. As a practical expedient we may occasionally account for group of performance obligations or contracts collectively, as opposed to individually by using the “portfolio approach” or the “series of distinct goods and services” method. Under the “portfolio approach” method, the Company may combine individual performance obligations, if the goods or services of the individual performance obligations have similar characteristics and the Company reasonably expects that the effect on the financial statements of applying this guidance would not defer materially from applying the guidance to the individual contracts or performance obligations within that portfolio. In addition, as a practical expedient, the Company does not assess the existence of a significant financing component when the difference between payment and transfer of control is less than one year. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: We attempt to identify, manage and mitigate risks to our business. However, some of these risks are not within our control, and risks and uncertainty cannot be fully eliminated or predicted. Prior to investing in our ordinary shares, you should carefully consider the following risk factors as well as other information contained in this annual report. The risk factors presented below may not necessarily be in order of importance or probability of occurrence. Risks Related to Our Operations A cyber or security attack or other similar incident resulting in a breach, disruption or failure in our or our supply chain's digital environment, or of our products, could adversely affect us. Our operations depend heavily on the continued and secure functioning of our varied digital environment software and hardware that stores, processes and transmits data within the Company and from and to us and our business partners. This digital environment is subject to breach, damage, destruction, disruption, malfunction or failure from, among other things, cyber-attacks and other unauthorized intrusions, power losses, telecommunications failures, acts of war or terror, earthquakes, fires and other natural disasters. We are continuously subjected to attempted cyber-attacks, ranging from standard phishing mails to sophisticated campaigns, such as spear phishing targeting specific Company management. While we have experienced an increase in the number of such threats and attempted cyber-attacks in recent years, which may be related to the geopolitical environment, none of these acts was believed to have had a material effect on the Company. Where required, relevant authorities were notified in accordance with the law and the relevant procedures the Company and its subsidiaries (as applicable) have in place. Our computer and communications systems, databases and users face ongoing threats of malicious software (malware), social engineering, distributed denial of service (DDoS), malicious code, zero-day vulnerabilities and other security threats and system disruptions carried out by a variety of threat actors. In particular, we have been and may continue to be targeted by nation states and experienced and skilled computer programmers and hackers, including those sponsored by or acting for foreign governments or terrorist organizations and in some cases, using artificial intelligence (AI), including generative AI and agentic AI to facilitate their attacks. Such programmers and hackers attempt to penetrate or circumvent our cyber security defenses, obtain data and damage or disrupt our digital environment in order to, among other things, misappropriate or compromise our IP or other proprietary or protected information or that of our employees, customers and other business partners, prevent us from being able to use such information in our operations or demand that we pay ransom. Our suppliers are also sometimes subject to cyber-attacks, which have increased in recent years and pose a risk to those of our systems and operations that depend on such suppliers. credit_strengths.text: Revenue and operating income have compounded steadily across the disclosed annual trend, with the latest year showing the strongest absolute earnings contribution. This defense-electronics franchise converts fixed-price long-term contracts into repeat revenue, and the rising operating margin sits above the sector median, indicating pricing discipline and mix improvement rather than volume-only growth.

The balance sheet carries a net cash position because unrestricted cash exceeds interest-bearing debt, and operating cash flow covers capital spending with a substantial surplus. Free cash flow relative to debt is exceptionally strong, and the cash conversion percentile versus Industrials peers is top-decile, supporting liquidity and refinancing flexibility.

key_risks.text: The disclosed risk factors highlight persistent and increasing cyber and supply-chain intrusions, including nation-state and AI-assisted campaigns, with a recent supplier incident. For a defense contractor holding sensitive intellectual property and customer data, a successful breach could disrupt operations, compromise programs and trigger contractual or regulatory consequences beyond the direct remediation cost.

Debt is almost entirely current long-term maturities, with only a small noncurrent portion, so the reported debt profile is short-dated and requires regular refinancing or repayment. Although the absolute debt burden is modest against cash generation, the maturity concentration means liquidity management and covenant access matter more than headline leverage suggests.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is comfortable but sits below the sector median, reflecting a meaningful gross interest expense relative to operating income. Because the company is net cash, reported interest expense likely includes non-debt items such as pension or lease-related charges; even so, coverage headroom is adequate but not peer-leading, and should be monitored as rates and debt mix evolve.

Free cash flow covers debt many times over, and the net cash position means refinancing risk is low in absolute terms. However, dividends absorb a meaningful share of free cash flow, so discretionary cash returned to shareholders competes with debt reduction and reinvestment; the maturity concentration in current debt still requires routine rollover capacity.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative financial risk profile is minimal, with net cash, strong free cash flow conversion and leverage far below the sector median. Operating momentum is positive across revenue, operating income and cash flow, and the Altman zone is grey rather than distressed. Analyst judgement: the credit trajectory is stable to improving, contingent on contract execution and cyber resilience.

Key sensitivities are the short-dated debt maturity profile, shareholder distributions consuming a large share of free cash flow, and elevated cyber and supply-chain risk inherent to defense contracting. The current ratio is only modestly above the sector median, so working-capital swings on long-term contracts could pressure liquidity. Analyst judgement: monitor refinancing and cyber disclosures rather than near-term solvency.

credit_strengths.text: 於已披露的年度趨勢中，收入及經營溢利均穩步複合增長，最近一年錄得最強的絕對盈利貢獻。此國防電子業務將固定價格長期合約轉化為重複收入，而上升的經營利潤率位於行業中位數之上，顯示定價紀律及組合改善，而非僅靠銷量增長。
資產負債表持有淨現金狀況，因為未受限現金超過計息債務，而經營現金流覆蓋資本開支後仍有大幅盈餘。自由現金流相對債務而言異常強勁，而現金轉換百分位相對於工業同業處於最高十分位，支持流動性及再融資靈活性。

key_risks.text: 已披露的風險因素凸顯持續且日益增加的網絡及供應鏈入侵，包括國家級及AI輔助的攻擊行動，近期亦發生供應商事件。對於持有敏感知識產權及客戶數據的國防承包商而言，成功的入侵可能中斷營運、危及項目，並引發合約或監管後果，超出直接補救成本。
債務幾乎全部為即期長期到期債務，僅有小部分為非即期，因此報告的債務狀況屬短期，需要定期再融資或償還。儘管相對於現金產生能力，絕對債務負擔不大，但到期集中意味著流動性管理及契約獲取比表面槓桿所顯示的更為重要。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率舒適，但低於行業中位數，反映相對於經營溢利而言，總利息支出有意義。由於公司處於淨現金狀況，報告的利息支出可能包括非債務項目，如退休金或租賃相關費用；即便如此，覆蓋率緩衝充足但並非同業領先，並應隨著利率及債務組合演變而監控。
自由現金流覆蓋債務多倍，而淨現金狀況意味著再融資風險在絕對值上較低。然而，股息佔用自由現金流中一個有意義的份額，因此返還股東的酌情現金與減債及再投資競爭；即期債務中的到期集中仍需要例行展期能力。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性財務風險狀況為極低，擁有淨現金、強勁的自由現金流轉換，以及遠低於行業中位數的槓桿。收入、經營溢利及現金流的營運勢頭均為正面，而Altman區域為灰色而非困境。分析師判斷：信貸軌跡穩定至改善，取決於合約執行及網絡韌性。
關鍵敏感因素為短期債務到期狀況、股東分派消耗自由現金流的一大部分，以及國防承包固有的高網絡及供應鏈風險。流動比率僅略高於行業中位數，因此長期合約的營運資金波動可能對流動性構成壓力。分析師判斷：監控再融資及網絡披露，而非近期償付能力。
